He previously led football organisations including Zenit Saint Petersburg and the Russian Football Union, then served in national sports and construction administration. His current work centres on housing finance, development programmes and urban policy.

long_biography.plain_text:
Water transport formed the starting point of Mutko's working life. After technical training, he joined the North-Western River Shipping Line, then entered municipal administration in Leningrad. His appointment as president of Zenit football club brought organisational leadership in sport to the centre of his career.

At the national federation, he oversaw Russian football before taking responsibility for sport at federal level. Construction, regional development and housing became his next portfolio. Mutko now serves as chief executive of DOM.RF, a publicly owned development institution active in mortgages, residential construction and urban projects. The position continues a career focused on directing large public organisations across different sectors.
long_biography.html:
Water transport formed the starting point of Mutko's working life. After technical training, he joined the North-Western River Shipping Line, then entered municipal administration in Leningrad. His appointment as president of Zenit football club brought organisational leadership in sport to the centre of his career.

At the national federation, he oversaw Russian football before taking responsibility for sport at federal level. Construction, regional development and housing became his next portfolio. Mutko now serves as chief executive of DOM.RF, a publicly owned development institution active in mortgages, residential construction and urban projects. The position continues a career focused on directing large public organisations across different sectors.

confidence.reason: The archived government biography supports the education, shipping, municipal and Zenit chronology; UEFA corroborates the football-management sequence; current DOM.RF and corporate-disclosure material establishes the present housing role.

Current official Russian sources use the patronymic Леонтьевич. Leontyevich is a standard English rendering consistent with English-language coverage, while Leontiyevich and Leontievich are noted transliteration variants.
Current DOM.RF group material names Vitaly Leontyevich Mutko as general director, and the 2025 re-election gives him a further five-year term.
The official Russian government biography states that Mutko was born in the Krasnodar Territory on 8 December 1958; Krasnodar Krai is the standard English administrative name.

uncertainties.detail: Russian official sources consistently give Леонтьевич. English sources variously render it as Leontyevich, Leontiyevich or Leontievich. The dossier proposes Leontyevich as a clear conventional English form while preserving Vitaly Mutko as the public display name.

The official biography places Mutko's birth in Krasnodar Territory in 1958, when it formed part of the Russian SFSR within the Soviet Union. Because the website's intended handling of historical-state versus modern-country labels is not established, birth_country remains unproposed.

The reliable public record reviewed here establishes employment, public office and leadership of state-owned or public institutions, but not a privately owned wealth platform. All four wealth classifications therefore remain Unknown; DOM.RF operations and assets are not attributed to Mutko personally.

The existing exact Wikipedia page remains valid. A historic press report described an official Instagram account, but no current canonical profile URL was verified; no LinkedIn, Instagram, personal website or Forbes profile is proposed.
Political detail beyond basic career identification, controversies, allegations, legal matters, sanctions, private-family material and vessel research are excluded.
